newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-FACTS ABOUT THE 1996 DAVIS CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FACTS ABOUT THE 1996 DAVIS CUP FINAL.

text.p: Facts about the 1996 Davis Cup final being played in Malmo between Sweden and France from November 29 to December 1.
Title - 84th Davis Cup final since the competition was inaugurated in 1900.
Venue - First time played in Malmo. Staged at the Convention Centre which is a converted ship building workshop and Saab plant with crowd capacity of 5,500. Fifth time played in Sweden.

Surface - Plexipave portable court surface. The sub-base is a "sandwich" wooden floor. The surface consists of multiple layers of Plexipave coatings. Sixth Davis Cup final to be played on a hard court with the previous five in 1969, 1970, 1971, 1978 and 1992. Davis Cup finals, including this year, have been played on grass - 53, clay - 16, carpet - nine, hard - six.
Indoor Davis Cup - It is the 18th Davis Cup final to be played indoors. Since the World Group began in 1981, 14 of the 16 World Group Finals have been played indoors.

Opponents - Sweden v France. It is the 11th meeting between the two nations in the history of the Davis Cup. Sweden leads the series 7-3. The two countries last played in 1994 at Cannes with Sweden defeating France 3-2.

Sweden - Entered the Davis Cup competition in 1925 and their 10th appearance in a Davis Cup final with a record of five wins to four defeats. The Swedes won in 1975 v Czechoslovakia, 1984 v U.S., 1985 v West Germany, 1987 v India, 1994 v Russia. In next year's competition Sweden will play at home to Switzerland in the opening round.
Swedish team - Captain Carl-Axel Hageskog. Players: Stefan Edberg, Thomas Enqvist, Nicklas Kulti, Jonas Bjorkman.

France - Entered the Davis Cup competition in 1904 and their 12th appearance in a Davis Cup final with a record of 7-4. The French won in 1927, 1928, 1929 and 1930 all v U.S., 1931 v Britain, 1932 and 1991 both v U.S. In next year's competition France will play away to Australia in the first round.
French team - Captain Yannick Noah. Players: Cedric Pioline, Arnaud Boetsch, Guy Forget, Guillaume Raoux.
Friday, Nov 29 - 1330 GMT Edberg v Pioline
Saturday, Nov 30 - 1500 GMT Kulti/Bjorkman v Forget/Raoux
